title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is an image manipulation failure inside a marketing and communications workflow. A photograph of real, identifiable students was edited with AI before it was placed on campus banners, and the edit changed the apparent race of one student and the apparent body size of others. The system was not making a decision or generating text. It was used to produce a synthetic version of a real event and real people, and that version was then published as if it depicted the event.

The failure was not caught because no human check stood between the edited file and the banner. Stanford's own policy prohibits using AI to change images of Stanford people and events, and the university has said both the alteration and the absence of disclosure violated it. Catching this would have required a review step that compared the published image against the original photograph and confirmed that any AI edit was disclosed, which the university's account indicates did not happen.

What is established is that Stanford acknowledged the AI alteration and called it a policy violation. What is not established from these reports is who performed the edit, what tool was used, or whether anyone intended the specific racial substitution, and the reports do not show that any individual has been found responsible.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior at Stanford, was photographed at a 2024 Lunar New Year event. When Stanford reused the image on campus banners, he had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students appeared thinner. Ramirez learned of the change from a friend and said being erased was upsetting.

Stanford acknowledged using artificial intelligence to alter the image. The university said its policy strictly prohibits using A.I. to change images of Stanford people and events, and that both the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises on additional training and proper review of materials.
